pairs: Altitudinis firmamentum pulchritudo ejus est,
The firmament on high is his beauty;
species cæli in visione gloriæ.
it is the beauty of heaven in a vision of glory.
Sol in aspectu annuntians in exitu,
The sun, at its appearance, announces its journey;
vas admirabile,
it is an instrument of wonder,
opus Excelsi.
a work of the Most High.
In meridiano exurit terram,
At midday, it scorches the earth.
et in conspectu ardoris ejus quis poterit sustinere?
And in the presence of its heat, who would be able to endure?
fornacem custodiens in operibus ardoris:
It is like the custodian of a furnace in its works of heat.
tripliciter sol exurens montes,
In three ways, the sun acts:
radios igneos exsufflans,
scorching the mountains, emitting fiery rays,
et refulgens radiis suis obcæcat oculos.
and shining with its beams that can blind the eyes.
Magnus Dominus qui fecit illum,
Great is the Lord who made it,
et in sermonibus ejus festinavit iter.
and at his word, it hurries on its journey.
Et luna in omnibus in tempore suo,
And the moon,
ostensio temporis,
in all its phases,
et signum ævi.
serves to mark the seasons and to be a sign of the times.
A luna signum diei festi:
From the moon is the sign of a feast day;
luminare quod minuitur in consummatione.
it is a light which diminishes at its consummation.
Mensis secundum nomen ejus est,
A month is named according to its phases,
crescens mirabiliter in consummatione.
increasing wonderfully at its culmination.
Vas castrorum in excelsis,
It is an instrument of the armies on high,
in firmamento cæli resplendens gloriose.
shining gloriously in the firmament of heaven.
Species cæli gloria stellarum:
The glory of the stars is the beauty of heaven;
mundum illuminans in excelsis Dominus.
the Lord illuminates the world from on high.
In verbis Sancti stabunt ad judicium,
At the words of the Holy One, they stand for judgment,
et non deficient in vigiliis suis.
and they will never fail in their vigilance.
Vide arcum,
Consider the rainbow,
et benedic eum qui fecit illum:
and bless the One who made it;
valde speciosus est in splendore suo.
it is very beautiful in its splendor.
Gyravit cælum in circuitu gloriæ suæ:
It encompasses the heavens with the circle of its glory;
manus Excelsi aperuerunt illum.
the hands of the Most High made it appear.
Imperio suo acceleravit nivem,
By his order, he hastens the snow,
et accelerat coruscationes emittere judicii sui.
and he spurs on the lightning to express his judgment.
Propterea aperti sunt thesauri,
In like manner, his storehouses are opened,
et evolaverunt nebulæ sicut aves.
and the clouds fly out like birds.
In magnitudine sua posuit nubes,
By his greatness, he has positioned the clouds,
et confracti sunt lapides grandinis.
and the hailstones have been broken.
In conspectu ejus commovebuntur montes,
At his glance, the mountains will be shaken,
et in voluntate ejus aspirabit notus.
and by his will, the south wind will blow.
Vox tonitrui ejus verberavit terram,
The voice of his thunder will reverberate through the earth,
tempestas aquilonis,
by a storm from the north,
et congregatio spiritus:
and by a gathering of the whirlwind.
et sicut avis deponens ad sedendum,
And like the birds landing in a flock upon the earth,
aspergit nivem,
he sends down the snow;
et sicut locusta demergens descensus ejus.
and its descent is like the arrival of a swarm of locusts.
Pulchritudinem candoris ejus admirabitur oculus,
The eye is in wonder at the beauty of its whiteness,
et super imbrem ejus expavescet cor.
and the heart is astonished at its falling.
Gelu sicut salem effundet super terram:
He will pour out frost like salt upon the earth.
et dum gelaverit,
And when it freezes,
fiet tamquam cacumina tribuli.
it will become like the tops of thistles.
Frigidus ventus aquilo flavit,
The cold north wind blows,
et gelavit crystallus ab aqua:
and the water freezes into crystals;
super omnem congregationem aquarum requiescet,
it will rest upon every gathering of water,
et sicut lorica induet se aquis:
and it will clothe the water like a breastplate.
et devorabit montes,
And it will devour the mountains,
et exuret desertum,
and burn the wilderness,
et extinguet viride,
and extinguish the greenery,
sicut igne.
like a fire.
Medicina omnium in festinatione nebulæ:
Relief for all is in the hurried arrival of a cloud.
et ros obvians ab ardore venienti humilem efficiet eum.
And the lowly dew will arrive to meet the heat and overpower it.
In sermone ejus siluit ventus,
At his word, the wind grows quiet,
et cogitatione sua placavit abyssum:
and by his thought, he appeases the abyss,
et plantavit in illa Dominus insulas.
for the Lord has planted islands in it.
Qui navigant mare enarrent pericula ejus,
Let those who navigate the sea describe its perils.
et audientes auribus nostris admirabimur.
And when we have heard it with our ears, we will wonder.
Illic præclara opera et mirabilia,
There are illustrious and wondrous works:
varia bestiarum genera,
the various kinds of wild animals,
et omnium pecorum,
and all manner of cattle,
et creatura belluarum.
and the great creatures of the sea.
Propter ipsum confirmatus est itineris finis,
Through him, the end of their journey is confirmed,
et in sermone ejus composita sunt omnia.
and by his word, all things fit together.
Multa dicemus,
We can say much,
et deficiemus in verbis:
and yet still lack for words.
consummatio autem sermonum ipse est in omnibus.
But the consummation of our words is this: He is in all things.
Gloriantes ad quid valebimus?
What would we be able to do to glorify him?
ipse enim omnipotens super omnia opera sua.
For the Almighty himself is above all his own works.
Terribilis Dominus,
The Lord is terrible,
et magnus vehementer,
and exceedingly great,
et mirabilis potentia ipsius.
and his power is wonderful.
Glorificantes Dominum quantumcumque potueritis,
Glorify the Lord as much as you are able,
supervalebit enim adhuc:
yet still he will far exceed this.
et admirabilis magnificentia ejus.
For his magnificence is beyond wonder.
Benedicentes Dominum,
Bless the Lord and exalt him,
exaltate illum quantum potestis:
as much as you are able.
major enim est omni laude.
But he is beyond all praise.
Exaltantes eum,
When you exalt him,
replemini virtute,
use all your ability,
ne laboretis,
and do not cease in this labor.
non enim comprehendetis.
For you can never comprehend him.
Quis videbit eum
Who will see him and explain?
et enarrabit?
And who will magnify him,
et quis magnificabit eum sicut est ab initio?
as he is from the beginning?
Multa abscondita sunt majora his:
There are many things, hidden from us, which are greater than these things.
pauca enim vidimus operum ejus.
For we have seen but a few of his works.
Omnia autem Dominus fecit,
But the Lord has made all things,
et pie agentibus dedit sapientiam.
and he has given wisdom to those who act with piety.
